label: COMPREHEND_1: a primitive relation, knowing a being as perfectly as it is knowable
term: comprehend (comprehendere, ST I q.12 a.7; Lean `Comprehension.Comprehends`)
definition: PRIMITIVE. Comprehends x y: x knows y as perfectly as y is knowable. After ST I q.12 a.7, where to comprehend is to know a thing perfectly, that is, as much as it is knowable. Example: a mathematician who knows a theorem by its demonstration comprehends it (the example of q.12 a.7, as against holding it as probable on authority). Counterexample: a person who knows truly that the theorem holds without knowing it by demonstration knows it but does not comprehend it. Distinguished from knowing y (truly, but not perfectly) and from attaining or seeing y, which q.12 a.7 ad 1 grants to the blessed with respect to God without comprehension; distinguished also from the propositional Knows of the veracity vocabulary (NamingVeracityBatch1: a being holds a proposition as known), which relates a knower to a proposition, not to a being.
note: Explicitly identified primitive (Encode first), introduced because the corpus had no relation between a knower and a known being. It is COMPREHEND_1 (disambiguation e151d506). Its gloss now has a typed sibling, COMPREHEND_2 (ComprehendsByMeasure, definition 1218cc1e: knowing at a degree that reaches the degree of knowability, with a degree of act and a power of knowing on one scale), and the bridge 'No intellect that is not INFINITE_1 comprehends an INFINITE_1 being' is derived from four open premises about those measures plus the open sense bridge 'Whatever COMPREHEND_1s a being COMPREHEND_2s it' (ComprehensionByMeasure). The two senses are not identified; that sense bridge is the only passage between them. Constraints placed on it: that bridge and, on the measured route, the sense bridge. Structural properties: none built in (not assumed reflexive, transitive or asymmetric; control part 1 of DeiFiliusImmenseIncomprehensible has a being that comprehends itself).
